measurement: free -m "used" (total - available) after login into XFCE with no apps open, 60 s after the panel appears; same figure `lindos-tune status` prints as the verdict line.
honesty: Every figure below is an ESTIMATE from component RSS measurements and upstream numbers until it has been measured on the Lindos reference machines (see docs/RAM-BUDGET.md for the measurement log). Savings overlap and do not simply add up.

baselines.name: Stock Linux Mint 22 XFCE (idle after login)
baselines.note: Mint 22.x XFCE, default session, mintupdate/mintreport/blueman trays, cups+bluetooth+ModemManager on, no zram.

baselines.name: Lindos 1.0 Everyday
baselines.note: picom on, zram 50 %, debloat presets, tray delayed.

baselines.name: Lindos 1.0 Lite
baselines.note: no compositor, zram 100 %, minimal tray, bluetooth/ModemManager/cups-browsed off, earlyoom -m 8.

measures.name: XFCE session instead of Cinnamon
measures.how: Base is Linux Mint XFCE (xfwm4 + xfce4-panel), not Cinnamon/muffin + nemo-desktop.
measures.explanation: Cinnamon idles around 800-950 MB, XFCE around 600-750 MB on the same Mint release. Already part of the base image; listed so the comparison to 'Mint' is fair.

measures.name: No compositor in Lite (no picom, xfwm compositing off)
measures.how: lindos-compositor honours COMPOSITOR=none from /etc/lindos/tune.d/lite.conf; xfwm4 use_compositing=false.
measures.explanation: picom (glx backend) holds ~20-30 MB plus GPU buffers per window; xfwm4 compositing another few MB. Also removes vsync latency on very old GPUs.
measures.reversible: lindos-mode set everyday (or Lindos Settings > Home > Compositor)

measures.name: Lite only: bluetooth.service disabled + blueman-applet hidden
measures.how: Lite mode's own /etc/lindos/tune.d/lite.conf SERVICES_DISABLE (and mode.json) + autostart-hide.list (blueman-applet if-disabled=bluetooth.service). The systemd preset 90-lindos.preset ENABLES bluetooth.service by default (SPEC §8) because laptops need Bluetooth headphones/mice; it is cheap when idle.
measures.explanation: bluetoothd ~5-8 MB, blueman-applet (python3 + GTK) ~12-18 MB. Only Lite mode (aimed at ≤4 GB RAM / old PCs) trades Bluetooth away for the saving; every other mode keeps it on by default, and the package stays installed so a single command restores it (see 'reversible').

measures.name: CUPS socket/path activated instead of always-on; cups-browsed disabled
measures.how: preset: disable cups.service, enable cups.socket + cups.path; disable cups-browsed.service.
measures.explanation: cupsd (~8-10 MB) starts on the first print job through cups.socket, cups-browsed (~4 MB, network printer discovery via avahi) is off; avahi-daemon itself stays on so printers are still found when you open the printer dialog.

measures.name: ModemManager disabled
measures.explanation: Only needed for built-in WWAN/3G/4G modems. Users with a mobile modem re-enable it (Lindos Settings > Network shows the hint).

measures.name: avahi-daemon KEPT enabled (documented, not a saving)
measures.how: preset: enable avahi-daemon.service (SPEC Â§8: keep for printer discovery).
measures.explanation: avahi uses ~3-4 MB; disabling it would save that but break network printer and .local discovery, so Lindos keeps it. Listed for transparency.

measures.name: apport, whoopsie, kerneloops, ubuntu-report disabled
measures.how: preset disable list + autostart-hide.list (apport, whoopsie autostart entries).
measures.explanation: Crash uploaders and telemetry that Lindos never sends anywhere: whoopsie ~5 MB resident, kerneloops ~2 MB, apport hooks. Nothing is lost for the user.

measures.name: NetworkManager-wait-online.service disabled
measures.explanation: No RAM saving; removes up to 30-60 s of boot delay when Wi-Fi is slow to associate. Listed because it is in the debloat list.

measures.name: brltty and speech-dispatcher disabled by default
measures.how: preset: disable brltty.service, speech-dispatcher.service; autostart-hide.list hides orca-autostart.
measures.explanation: Braille display and speech daemons only help users who need them; brltty also grabs some USB serial adapters (Arduino/ESP boards). Accessibility users re-enable them in Settings.

measures.name: mintwelcome/mintreport tray hidden; mintupdate tray kept
measures.how: autostart-hide.list: mintwelcome (replaced by lindos-setup OOBE), mintreport (System Reports tray). mintupdate stays (its own autostart delays 90 s).
measures.explanation: mintwelcome ~15-20 MB (python3 + WebKit view) at every login, mintreport-tray ~10 MB polling for crash reports. mintupdate's tray is kept: it is how users learn about updates; it starts late so the early idle measurement is ~20 MB lower.
measures.reversible: remove NotShowIn=XFCE; from /etc/xdg/autostart/mintreport.desktop (or copy the entry to ~/.config/autostart)

measures.name: zram compressed swap (50 % / 75 % gaming / 100 % lite of RAM, zstd)
measures.explanation: Not an idle-RAM saving (zram itself costs a few hundred KB until used) but it turns 4 GB into 'feels like 6-7 GB' by compressing idle anonymous pages ~3:1 in RAM instead of hitting the disk. Effective headroom on 4 GB: +1.5-2.5 GB.

measures.name: journald capped at 64 MB persistent (8 MB files, 32 MB runtime)
measures.explanation: journald mmaps its active journal files; huge journals mean more page cache and slower boots. 64 MB keeps about a week of desktop logs. Storage stays persistent for bug reports.

measures.name: /tmp on tmpfs (tmp.mount)
measures.how: systemctl enable tmp.mount (fallback: fstab tmpfs line, size=50%).
measures.explanation: Uses RAM only for what is actually in /tmp (nothing at idle); saves SSD writes and speeds up installers/Wine temp files. Big /tmp users are covered by zram swap.

measures.name: earlyoom (-m 4, Lite -m 8) protects the desktop
measures.explanation: Costs ~1 MB. Kills the biggest offender (usually a browser tab process) before the kernel OOM freezes the whole desktop for minutes on 4 GB machines.

measures.name: No file indexers or preloaders
measures.how: Base image ships no tracker/baloo/recoll/preload; ananicy-cpp rules push updatedb/man-db/timeshift to idle priority.
measures.explanation: Desktop search indexers keep 30-80 MB resident and thrash the disk after login. Lindos uses plain Thunar search + catfish on demand.
measures.reversible: install what you like (apt install plocate)

measures.name: snapd not present
measures.how: Linux Mint already ships without snapd (pinned); Flatpak is used instead and adds no daemon.
measures.explanation: Listed because Ubuntu-based comparisons often include snapd (~25 MB + loop mounts). Not a Lindos saving relative to Mint.

measures.name: vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50, dirty ratios 10/5, page-cluster 0
measures.explanation: Keeps directory/inode cache warmer and writes dirty pages sooner so a big copy does not stall the UI. Neutral for idle RAM.

measures.name: LightDM + slick-greeter kept (already light)
measures.how: No change; slick-greeter exits after login, lightdm ~4 MB.
measures.explanation: GDM/SDDM would cost 20-60 MB more. Nothing to gain by switching.

measures.name: Lite: minimal tray (no clipman, no notes/weather plugins, no power-manager tray)
measures.how: modes/lite panel profile (lindos-desktop) â€” outside lindos-tune, listed for the budget total.
measures.explanation: Every panel plugin is a GTK object tree; the Lite profile keeps whisker, docklike, systray, audio, clock only.
